images.filename: Lockheed OP-2E Neptune of VO-67 in flight on a mission over Laos, circa in 1967.jpg
images.caption: A U.S. Navy Lockheed OP-2E Neptune (BuNo 131423) of Observation Squadron 67 (VO-67) on a mission over Laos in 1967-68. VO-67 was employed during the "Igloo White" programme to drop sensors along the "Ho Chi Minh Trail" to detect movements of enemy troops during the Vietnam War.
images.alt: A U.S. Navy Lockheed OP-2E Neptune (BuNo 131423) of Observation Squadron 67 (VO-67) on a mission over Laos in 1967-68. VO-67 was employed during the "Igloo White" programme to drop sensors along the "Ho Chi Minh Trail" to detect movements of enemy troops during the Vietnam War.

images.caption:
The commissioned officers living quarters, dubbed "The Womb", was destroyed during the siege of Khe Sanh in 1968.  The caption on this photograph notes that all occupants were on duty at when the bunker was destroyed and no one was injured.  The caption also states that the ruined bunker was used "to store the remaining brandy."

From the John M. Kaheny Collection (COLL/99) at the Marine Corps Archives & Special Collections.
